title: Jenna Ortega Says She Hopes ‘Klara and the Sun’ Encourages People to ‘Put Down the Computers and Phones’ as Dystopian Film World Premieres in London
content:
Jenna Ortegahopes that her new film, the dystopian sci-fi “Klara and the Sun,” can remind people to live in the moment in the age of AI and all-consuming technology.

“I think we gotta put our focus on one another and put down the computers and phones,” the star toldVarietyon the red carpet at the movie’s world premiere atLondon Film Festivalon Thursday night.

Ortega, wearing a stunning yellow lace dress and hair piece, added: “Remember to be present and to appreciate people while they’re standing right in front of you.”

Based on Nobel Prize winner Kazuo Ishiguro’s bestselling 2021 novel of the same name, “Klara and the Sun” is set in a future where advances in genetic engineering have divided humans into strict social classes. Ortega plays Klara, an artificial android companion who is purchased for an ailing girl named Josie (Mia Tharia). “Klara and the Sun” is directed by “Thor” helmer Taika Waititi and also starsAmy Adamsas Josie’s mother, Aran Murphy (son of Cillian Murphy), Natasha Lyonne, Steve Buscemi and more.

Waititi, Adams, Murphy and Lyonne all walked the London Film Festival red carpet on Thursday night, alongside Waititi’s wife Rita Ora, author Ishiguro and a surprise appearance from Florence Pugh, who stunned in a blue floral gown with statement sleeves. Pugh enthusiastically greeted Ortega and Adams before they all posed for photos together alongside producer Rachel Forman.

Standing alongside Ortega, Adams added that everyone she’s spoken to has gotten “something different” out of the film. “That, to me, is a really successful film that communicates something different to each viewer. So I like hearing what people get out of it,” she said.

Ortega clarified that though Klara is an “artificial friend,” she doesn’t work like the AI that we know today.

“AI I guess pulls all this information from the internet and Klara gets all her information from the real world,” she said. “So that’s a little bit different. She’s kind of like a toddler in a sense. Playing her specifically in this film was really interesting because Taika wanted a more human approach, so he didn’t want to do movement that was too robotic, maybe more sort of clumsy and unknowing.”

Waititi echoed Ortega in saying that the film’s message is to “put the phone down.”

“I would just like people to remember what friendship is, connect with people and just be,” he said. “Just be in the moment.”

Ishiguro acknowledged that, since his novel came out in 2021, the world’s awareness and attitude about AI has changed greatly.

“This film doesn’t address a lot of the anxieties that you and I may have right now about where we’re going with the technology. I mean, I think quite rightly, it’s really come center stage,” he said. “I’m aware that this film is coming out into a very different world to the one that my novel came out in five years ago, and I don’t know how that will change people’s expectations or how people look at things. But I’ll say that this isn’t another film about how an AI machine seems to be nice and then becomes sinister and ends up killing all the nice people in the film. It’s not that sort of story.”

Ishiguro is wading more into film, confirming toVarietythat he’s working on a new project with Tim Burton, for which he penned an original script. Though Burton and Ishiguro have a mutual friend in “Wednesday” star Ortega, he said she’s not the one who introduced them.

“I thought this was supposed to be a big secret!” Ishiguro said. “No, Jenna didn’t introduce us. Tim lives quite near where I live in North London, and I was dropping in on him in his very strange and wacky and beautiful house. I mean, it looks like a Tim Burton set. And we started to talk about a project and I wrote a script on spec. We decided to just do it privately between the two of us, and then take it to people.”

He added that it’s not a “war film,” saying: “Genre-wise, it’s very hard to pigeonhole. It’s a Tim Burton film!”

“Klara and the Sun” is set to hit theaters via Sony Pictures on Oct. 23.
title_zh: 珍娜·奧爾蒂嘉(Jenna Ortega)表示，她希望《克拉拉與陽光》(Klara and the Sun)能鼓勵人們「放下電腦和手機」，因為這部反烏托邦電影在倫敦首映。
content_zh:
珍娜·奧特嘉(Jenna Ortega)希望她的新片反烏托邦科幻電影《克拉拉與陽光》(Klara and the Sun)能提醒人們在人工智慧和無所不在的科技時代中活在當下。

這位明星在週四晚上於倫敦電影節的全球首映紅毯上告訴《綜藝》(Variety)：“我認為我們應該把重心放在彼此身上，放下電腦和手機。”

奧特嘉身穿一襲驚豔的黃色蕾絲裙和髮飾，補充道：“記得要活在當下，珍惜那些就在你面前的人。”

《克拉拉與陽光》改編自諾貝爾獎得主石黑一雄(Kazuo Ishiguro)於2021年出版的暢銷小說，故事設定在一個基因工程進步的未來，將人類劃分為嚴格的社會階級。奧特嘉在片中飾演克拉拉，一位被購買來陪伴一位名叫喬茜(Mia Tharia)的病女孩的人工智能伴侶。《克拉拉與陽光》由《雷神》(Thor)導演泰卡·維提提(Taika Waititi)執導，還有艾米·亞當斯(Amy Adams)飾演喬茜的母親、阿蘭·墨菲(Aran Murphy，基利安·墨菲(Cillian Murphy)之子)、娜塔莎·里昂(Natasha Lyonne)、史提夫·布西密(Steve Buscemi)等人聯袂演出。

維提提、亞當斯、墨菲和里昂在週四晚上一同走上倫敦電影節的紅毯，還有維提提的妻子麗塔·歐拉(Rita Ora)、作家石黑一雄以及驚喜現身的佛羅倫斯·皮尤(Florence Pugh)，她身穿藍色花卉長裙，袖子引人注目。皮尤熱情地向奧特嘉和亞當斯打招呼，然後他們一起與製片人瑞秋·福爾曼(Rachel Forman)合影。

亞當斯在奧特嘉身旁補充說，她所接觸的每個人對這部電影都有“不同的感受”。“對我來說，這是一部非常成功的電影，能夠向每位觀眾傳達不同的東西。所以我喜歡聽聽人們從中獲得了什麼，”她說。

奧特嘉澄清，雖然克拉拉是一位“人工朋友”，但她的運作方式與我們今天所知的人工智慧不同。

“人工智慧我想是從互聯網上提取所有這些信息，而克拉拉則是從現實世界獲取她的所有信息，”她說。“所以這有點不同。她在某種程度上就像一個幼兒。在這部電影中專門飾演她真的很有趣，因為泰卡想要一種更人性化的方式，所以他不想讓她的動作過於機械化，而是更笨拙和無知。”

維提提呼應奧特嘉的說法，表示這部電影的訊息是“放下手機”。

“我希望人們能記得友誼是什麼，與他人聯繫，並且只是存在，”他說。“活在當下。”

石黑一雄承認，自從他的小說於2021年出版以來，世界對人工智慧的認識和態度已經發生了很大變化。

“這部電影並沒有解決你我目前對科技未來的焦慮。我是說，我認為這是非常正確的，它真的已經成為焦點，”他說。“我知道這部電影將在一個與我五年前小說發表時截然不同的世界中上映，我不知道這將如何改變人們的期望或人們看待事物的方式。但我可以說，這不是另一部關於人工智慧機器看似友好然後變得陰險，最後殺死電影中所有好人的故事。這不是那種故事。”

石黑一雄(Ishiguro)正在更深入地涉足電影，向《綜藝》(Variety)確認他正在與蒂姆·波頓(Tim Burton)合作一個新項目，並為此撰寫了一部原創劇本。儘管波頓和石黑有共同的朋友，即《星期三》(Wednesday)的明星奧爾特加(Ortega)，但他表示奧爾特加並不是介紹他們的人。

“我以為這應該是一個大秘密！”石黑說。“不，珍娜(Jenna)並沒有介紹我們。蒂姆住在我在北倫敦的家附近，我曾經去他那個非常奇特、古怪而美麗的房子拜訪他。我是說，那看起來就像是一個蒂姆·波頓(Tim Burton)的片場。我們開始談論一個項目，我寫了一個自發的劇本。我們決定在我們兩人之間私下進行，然後再帶給其他人。”

他補充說，這不是一部“戰爭電影”，並表示：“從類型上來說，很難歸類。這是一部蒂姆·波頓(Tim Burton)的電影！”

《克拉拉與太陽》(Klara and the Sun) 預定於10月23日由索尼影業(Sony Pictures)上映。
